physicalNotes: Radius 1.17 ± 0.08 Earth radii from Torres et al. 2015 (ApJ 800, 99 (2015); arXiv:1501.01101), at 6378.137 km per Earth radius. No mass is measured, so no gravitational parameter is adopted. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.shape: Inclination 89.96 degrees and a/R* = 178 (+65/-21) from Torres et al. (2015), Table 8. Eccentricity is set to 0: a circular display approximation, not an orbital solution.
sources.phase: Torres et al. 2015, Table 8, column KOI-0571.05: tau = BJD_UTC 2455789.4940 (the paper gives the time in UTC, not TDB; the difference of about a minute is not applied).
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
